text:
john_cust: Hey support — we're seeing EventSource streams from Redwood intermittently stall in Safari behind our CDN. Client gets a partial event, then the connection drops and the browser reconnects and sometimes replays the partial chunk. Happens only in Safari desktop + iOS. We've captured some headers that show `Accept-Encoding: br` on the client side via our edge. Any obvious causes?
support-bot: Thanks for reporting — can you share a sample request id or a minimal repro? Also include the response headers around the last successful and failed attempts. :eyes:
maya: Hi — from past issues this smells like edge-level compression / 304 handling altering chunk boundaries. Does your CDN send `Content-Encoding: br` on the 200 but omit it on 304/keepalive responses?
john_cust: repro steps: 1) open page in Safari 16 on macOS Big Sur 2) start stream -> endpoint `https://streams.prod.redwood.example/ev?room=123` 3) after ~30s you see `event: message\ndata: {"partial":true` then connection stalls. We also see occasional 304 from edge during revalidation. Headers (snip):
```
Accept: text/event-stream
Accept-Encoding: br, gzip
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7)
```
Response headers (last attempt):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Content-Encoding: br
Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, s-maxage=60
Vary: Accept-Encoding, Origin
X-Request-ID: rq_01F5KX...
```
then later a 304 for the same resource with fewer headers.
kevin: If the edge returns a 304 and the browser expects streaming body but the 304 has no body, Safari can get confused if the polyfill or native EventSource expects a continuous byte stream. Brotli + edge revalidation is a common trigger. CDNs sometimes remove `Content-Encoding` or change `Content-Length` on 304 which breaks mid-stream.
sam: Quick mitigation to try: set `Cache-Control: no-transform` (prevents edge from recompressing) and ensure `Vary: Accept-Encoding` is correct. Also for SSE endpoints we recommend `Cache-Control: private, no-transform, max-age=0, must-revalidate` to avoid intermediate caching altering bytes.
maya: Another defensive option: make SSE responses include `Cache-Control: no-store` or add a cache-bypass query param for streams to avoid any 304 paths. If customers need CDN in front for other reasons, ensure the CDN honors `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and does not buffer to revalidate.
john_cust: any quick client workaround? We're constrained — many users hit this in production.
kevin: Client-side workarounds are limited for native EventSource. If you control the page, consider using fetch+ReadableStream to implement a streaming client (more robust to chunking changes) or use an SSE polyfill that handles mid-stream reconcat better. Example fetch approach: 
```js
const res = await fetch(url, {headers: {Accept: 'text/event-stream'}});
const reader = res.body.getReader();
// read loop and parse events manually
```
This avoids Safari's EventSource parser quirks.
sam: Also check service worker and prefetch settings — Safari may prefetch and then reuse the connection differently. Disable `link rel=prefetch` or test with service worker disabled.
maya: Can you also capture the x-request-id `rq_01F5KX...` for the failed attempt and send server side logs? Eng-runtime can check whether KV cache flipping or kernel selection caused a short response. :thumbsup:
john_cust: sending logs + last x-request-id now. Appreciate quick triage.
support-bot: Filed internal ticket #SUP-4221, tagging eng-runtime. Will update when we have root cause.
kevin: FYI we have a known issue tracked where Brotli + CloudFront revalidation can remove chunked framing on 304 leading to Safari stalls. Fix in progress but for now CDN config + no-transform is the fastest mitigation.
maya: If you want, we can temporarily roll a small edge rule to avoid brotli for `/ev` prefix and test.
john_cust: let's try that, thanks — can you put the edge rule in staging first?
sam: I'll coordinate with infra on a short-lived edge config change in staging and report back. :white_check_mark: 
kevin: tagging @eng-runtime to look for metrics spikes and to correlate request ids.
eng-runtime: on it, will check buffering and early EOF patterns in logs once you post the traces.
support-bot: closing loop once eng-runtime confirms. Thanks everyone.
